event: Wren wakes on Day 28 to Brecca repointing the low retaining wall around the threshold stone.
Brecca's hands pause longer on each joint now, practicing toward a standard from the ridge.
She does not announce it or explain it. She works.
At the dawn vibration the bond returns as the full three-node chord after two days of thread.
She rereads three pages of expedition survey notes written the night before.
She starts a return expedition plan: structures, notation, junctions, the well, the ring.
She stops, hearing her mother: without turning it into a project.
The plan has no line for Theron's silence or Brecca's reverence or the taste of the water.
The plan is necessary and insufficient; she closes the journal and sits with the stone.
The morning passes in rhythm: Brecca between the retaining wall and the hall's west face.
At midday Wren finds Theron studying the terrain past the channel's south end.
'The gradient continues': a faint depression runs south toward the perimeter.
'I want to clear what is already there. This is not maintenance. This is recovery.'
Wren tells him the southern drainage was a network. 'Yes. I know.'
One channel was one sentence; Theron is learning to read the paragraph. He starts clearing.
At mid-afternoon Wren sits at the threshold stone, its signature resolving through Journeyman eyes.
She lays Detail Notation on the east face; the mark sinks and merges with the signature.
The twelve bands resolve into composition: iron-rich, silica-dense, calcite-threaded.
The stone is a geological journal, each band a period of the formation's history.
In the seventh, iron-richest band she feels the southern foundation's quality: intention.
Someone once deepened that one band with a single touch, centuries ago.
A discovery logs band 7's trace reinforcement: +55 XP, Surveying to 65.

changes.note: Discovery: threshold stone band 7 carries the southern reinforcement

event: 'The thread connects': the tradition is older than the masons who dressed this stone.
Not an answer, a thread, running between the places through stone and hands.
Brecca finds her: 'You are doing the face again.' 'Discovery.'
Wren explains plainly: twelve bands, one like the southern foundations. Someone touched it.
Brecca lays her hand on the seventh band: 'Show me.'
Wren marks the band with Detail Notation; the surface shimmers faintly.
'The stone is warmer there. Like someone held their hand here a very long time.'
'That is what I feel too,' Wren says.
Brecca declares she will keep repointing all of it, where she meets the tradition.
She goes back to the gathering hall; Wren watches her go.
At the evening fire Wren writes to her mother on her good paper.
Theron digs the drainage south in the tree line; Brecca has circled the whole hall in a day.
The three-person fire is quieter; they wait for Hadley without saying so.
She tells Dad the six-degree gradient works here.
She writes of the ruined town south, and of Brecca, who does not know she is remarkable.
'I should have sent a sentence. I am learning.' She writes of Theron, who just clears.
She is trying not to make people a project; the rosemary still smells, fainter.
She writes of stones made more than stone, and that she is learning to sit with questions.
'Tell Dad: the map is bigger than he thinks. -- W.' She folds it into her journal for Hadley.
Hadley arrives mid-morning on Day 29, alone, narrating the trail, carrying fresh supplies.
'Maret is coming. Not today. She said three days. She has things to bring.'
Maret questioned him two hours: the stone, the pulse, the drainage, Brecca, Wren.
Her message: 'I am bringing what she needs. She does not know she needs it yet.'
Told of the southern settlement, Maret went quiet and said: 'They found it.'
Hadley thinks she has been waiting a long time for someone to find it.
Maret arrives Day 32, four days before the pulse. 'She is cutting it close.'
'She is cutting it exactly where she means to,' Hadley says.
The evening fire is four again; Hadley cooks dried fish, foraged greens and salt.
Wren gives Hadley the letter for her mother; he tucks it in his own journal unasked.
Brecca found thumb-impressions pressed in a repeating sequence into the retaining wall's clay.
'Like the niche. Hidden until you do the work.' 'Except this has someone's thumbs in it.'
Theron looks at his own hands: the mason was his grandmother's mother.
The extended channel carries a thin trickle south; the settlement holds and grows.
She journals 'Day 29. Eleven. Hadley returned. Maret coming Day 32.' Not the pulse, seven days off.
The count climbs; to the south, through the limestone, the thread holds.
